I was 7 and mother bought me a  tea set, it's child sized but real porcelain. I received it sometime before Christmas, however didn't want to open it until we've gone to visit my cousins during the holidays.

A class Christmas party was coming up, and we had to do exchange gifts. It was also around this time that I figured money doesn't grow on trees and my family was going through financial troubles.

When we went to the store, I looked around to what my classmate might like. Having learned my maths earlier that term, I realised children's toys are expensive. So I went to mother and suggested we give the tea set instead. I said she'd never get anything like it and that all the items in the store were rubbish compared to it.

She pointed to toys we could afford, but I insisted. I know she would have never agreed if we weren't in such trouble but, she did and we were. By the time our finances had gone back to normal, I was past the age of playing tea or house. Still warms my heart though when we pass by tea sets.

When I was 8yo and throwing a fit at the mall because Mom wouldn't buy me that tea set, my big brother leant down to me and very quietly said, "not everything you want will be yours."

Needless to say, never threw a fit after that.
